summary: Carefully preregistered, well-executed paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) comparing a selective low-latency verification intervention against LLM-only generation on a 400-item synthetic NetOps corpus. All primary artifacts (per-episode JSONs, validator traces, provider-call logs, execution manifest, analysis outputs) are archived with SHA-256 hashes. Primary result: baseline valid = 399/400, guarded valid = 400/400; paired difference = 0.0025, exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0, paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0075]. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2) could not be evaluated because end-to-end latency telemetry is absent; this omission is disclosed in the manuscript and execution logs. Analysis and deterministic reconciliation are internally consistent and artifact-backed. I find the experimental execution and reporting to be reproducible and appropriately cautious; no unresolved critical defects remain that must be corrected before finalisation.
optional_revisions: Add (or point to) a small per-episode worked example of the single discordant pair (n10=1) in the main text or appendix and cite its scorer/validator JSON path to aid readers’ failure-mode inspection (artifact-backed).

Explicitly label the primary estimand as conditional on the preregistered shared-initial generation (i.e., clarify that the effect size estimates verifier/repair impact given a shared candidate) and move any remaining estimand/interpretation text into a single concise paragraph in Methods for readers.

Expand Limitations to discuss the ceiling effect and its consequence for power and practical interpretation (the synthetic corpus yielded near-ceiling baseline performance, reducing observed room for verifier gains).

Make the execution-manifest path and the single-file hashes referenced in the Disclosure Statement clickable or formatted as monospace in the compiled manuscript to ease artifact inspection (formatting only; no new data).

For transparency, attach a one-paragraph note in the manuscript describing why planned_model_calls was enumerated as 800 in the preregistration while the executed shared-initial design produced 401 model calls, and point readers to the exact execution_manifest entries that reconcile these counts (artifact SHA-256 already present).
